content: Ilex guayusa, commonly referred to as guayusa, is a tree belonging to the holly genus and is indigenous to the Ecuadorian Amazon Rainforest. It is botanically related to Yerba Mate and Yaupon Holly, the latter being the plant traditionally used to prepare the black drink. Among all known plants, the leaves of guayusa contain the highest concentration of caffeine. These leaves are typically boiled to prepare a tea, and due to their exceptionally high caffeine content, the same leaves can be reused multiple times, often over the course of several days. Both fresh and dried leaves are utilized for this purpose. The dried leaves are often rolled and strung together in a manner resembling a Hawaiian lei. Beyond its stimulant properties, guayusa tea is traditionally consumed to enhance the recall of dreams. To achieve this effect, it is believed that the tea must be consumed consistently in the early morning, immediately after waking and before sunrise. For many indigenous communities in Ecuador, the morning consumption of guayusa tea is a deeply ingrained social ritual. In regions where the plant grows, guayusa is also commonly included as an additive in the preparation of ayahuasca, a potent entheogenic brew. It is used either alongside the more typical DMT-containing plants or as a substitute for them. Indigenous Ecuadorian people also claim that guayusa, when consumed in sufficiently high quantities, exhibits mild hallucinogenic properties on its own. Guayusa is commercially available under the brand name Qat Tea™. However, it is important to note that this product is unrelated to the stimulant plant known as qat.
